## READ BEFORE ACTIVATING

Your n8n ALREADY RUNS a P0.2. This file is a rebuild, not a patch.

**Never leave both Active.** Two workflows writing the same tables is
worse than one.

Safe cutover:
  1. Import this. Leave it INACTIVE.
  2. Fill in Config.
  3. Run it once with the Manual Trigger (or the AD4 Workflows page).
  4. Compare its Summary line against your original's.
  5. Only then: deactivate the original, activate this.

## Run this ONCE with slug_template EMPTY

> The Polymarket endpoints here are **NOT reachable from the build machine** -
> that sandbox blocks polymarket.com - so the **first run** is the test. This
> mode exists precisely so the format comes from your account, not from a guess.

That is how it ships, and the first run is meant to fail. It will list what
Polymarket actually has and print the real slugs, like:

    highest-temperature-in-nyc-on-september-6   (11 buckets, first: 70-71F)

**Then copy one into `slug_template` in Config**, replacing the city with
`{city}`, the month with `{month}` and the day number with `{day}`:

    highest-temperature-in-{city}-on-{month}-{day}

If the city word in the real slug does not match your `city_key`, add a
mapping to `city_slug_overrides`, e.g. `{"new_york":"nyc"}`.

Run again and it will fetch exactly those events.

### Why it works this way

Listing and filtering did not work, three times. Gamma IGNORES query
parameters it does not recognise rather than rejecting them, so
`?limit=40&tag_slug=weather` returned **2160 events and 26 MB** of elections
and sports - and n8n fell over holding it. Every fix was another guess at a
parameter this repo cannot test: the machine that builds these files is
blocked from polymarket.com.

So the guessing is gone. A temperature market has a known slug, one per city
per day. We know the cities and the days, so each event is asked for by name.
One event per response, nothing to paginate, no tag taxonomy to be wrong
about. Placeholders: `{city} {month} {month_num} {day} {day_pad} {date} {year}`.

### What to check on the first successful run

**The settlement dates** the Summary prints. They come from `endDate` rolled
back a day when it lands before noon UTC, which is how these markets close. If
they are all one day out, that rule is one function at the top of
`Parse markets + bands`.

**"bucket label(s) unreadable"**. Polymarket states the bucket only as text -
"70-71F", "78F or above" - and a band with no numeric bounds cannot be priced
by anything. A handful is normal; most of them means the format moved, and the
run stops rather than writing a ladder with holes in it.
